newsitem.title: JAPAN: TOCOM PGM futures end mixed in volatile trade.
newsitem.headline: TOCOM PGM futures end mixed in volatile trade.

text.p: Yen-based platinum and palladium futures ended mixed on Tuesday after volatile trade, with nearby futures, excluding spot June, ending sharply higher.

Private investors rushed to cover their short-positions, amidst the extreme tightness in the physical market, sending most nearby contracts up to their daily price limits during the day, traders said.

"The PGM market is in chaos. TOCOM nearby months, distant months and spot prices moved in different directions. The forward market is not functioning properly and lease rates are not at appropriate levels," one trader said.
Spot June platinum tumbled by 76 yen per gram on heavy long-liquidation to end at 1,727 yen after surging on Monday.
Other platinum futures ranged from two yen to 50 yen per gram up, with benchmark April ending up two at 1,398 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from 29 yen per gram lower to 24 yen higher. Benchmark April was down 16 yen at 566 yen.

"Until supplies start flowing into the market, there is nothing we can do," the trader said. Some trade houses said they had signed documents with Russia's platinum group metal export agency for PGM deliveries starting in July. The agency earlier told clients PGM exports would resume in late June.

Four platinum futures contracts surged by their 50 yen per gram daily limit by midday and the wider gold/platinum spread prompted private investors to sell platinum futures and buy gold futures, another trader said.

Gold futures ended mostly lower on the yen's firmer tendency against the dollar, but bargain-hunting helped offset early losses. Gold futures ranged from unchanged to eight yen per gram lower. Benchmark April ended one yen weaker at 1,243 yen. Spot gold was quoted at $343.80/344.30 at 0805 GMT, against $344.00/50 in New York on Monday. Benchmark April silver was 0.7 yen per 10 grams easier at 175.4 yen.
